utterances.text: This is a villager in Plocica standing in front of his food warehouse burning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this building was built of?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously, the -- well, the roof is wood and tile, and the walls from the photograph looks like some form of stone and a thin plaster with wooden frames.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do we see any other structures that were part of this village which you say was terribly damaged?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you told us that you saw a plastic bottle that was used for petrol. Did you take a photograph of it?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe I did. I would have to check our photo archive to confirm that, but I believe we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you agree with me that that sort of photograph was not shown to you either today or yesterday in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right if I say that you also saw an empty bullet box there?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an empty ammunition box that I believe contained mortars, but I'm not sure about that. That's the best of my recollection. I seem to recall a mortar launcher next to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that we did not see a photograph depicting such an ammunition box either yesterday or today?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have a single piece of evidence to the effect that the Serbian Yugoslav authorities were receiving reports from -- or received a report from Human Rights Watch entitled "A Sunday of Terror in Drenica"?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: "A Week of Terror in Drenica."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm -- just to understand, confirmation that they received a copy of the report? Is that your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any information of that sort, no, although the -- I know that I gave multiple interviews to the various media in both English, Albanian, and Serbian language, and the report was covered widely. The incident in Obrinje was a very well-publicised event, the end of the campaign, and it sparked a flurry of diplomatic activity that led to the creation of an observer mission, and our views about that incident, our documentation, were widely publicised. So I always was firmly of the opinion that the Serbian public and government were aware of our findings. And I further recall media coverage in the RTS, the Radio Television Serbia, the official government media, that was directly refuting our claims, saying that the bodies -- the body of one of the victims, an 18-month-old victim named Valmir, if I'm correct, had been a doll. I remember that distinctly, them holding up a doll saying that this was what human rights organisations had claimed was the victim. So it was definitely broadcast in the state-run media.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Abrahams, I didn't want to interrupt you, but please look at your answer, and I urge you to answer my questions as briefly as possible. We do have a time-limit. In your testimony in the Milosevic case, in the Milutinovic case, and over the past two days, were you shown a single piece of evidence by the Prosecution to prove that this report entitled "A Week of Terror In Drenica" had been received by either the Serbian or the Yugoslav government?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That it had been delivered, yes; that it had been received, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I don't know, but it seems to me that the interpretation was excellent. My question was the following: Mr. Abrahams, in the Milosevic case, the Milutinovic case, and over the past two days, did the Prosecution show to you some evidence indicating that the Serbian or the Yugoslav governments received your report entitled "A Week of Terror In Drenica"?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now call up P754, page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Abrahams, do you recognise the photograph?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It seems to me that you said that you were the one who took it.

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I also think you said that it was in February of 1999; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us what village this is?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lodja.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us, how many houses does the village of Lodja have?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you precisely. I remember approximately three dozen, maybe a bit more -- more, I think, but I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you agree with me that, again, we don't have a long shot that would depict the village of Lodja?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have many photos of Lodja. This one here depicts two houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know how many Serb houses there were in the village of Lodja in February of 1999 when you took the photograph?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean by "Serb house"?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, you told us a moment ago how many houses there were. Of course I'm not referring to houses themselves. I'm referring to households.

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Right. Let's say, how many Albanian houses were there in the village of Lodja, i.e., members of Albanian ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the precise ethnic composition of Lodja, but my understanding is it was a predominantly, if not exclusively, ethnic Albanian-inhabited village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you try at all to establish whether there was any Serb population in the village when you were there back in February?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In February 1999, the village was uninhabited.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So how come you're able to know who -- to whom the houses depicted in the photograph belonged? How were you able to tell if they belonged to members of the Serb ethnicity or Albanian ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We tried to enter Lodja first in September 1998 and were denied. We wanted to go there and interview individuals who we believed were ethnic Albanians, that ethnic Albanians lived in Lodja, but we were denied entry into the village by the Serbian police who had occupied a home or structure, a building, on the edge of the village. Based on that, it was my belief and opinion that the village was predominantly, if not exclusively, inhabited by ethnic Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Abrahams, you're giving me long answers without answering my question. The question was: How were you able to tell or know in February of 1999 when you took these photographs who the owners of the houses were and of which ethnicity the owners were?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, that question has been answered. It may not be the answer you were expecting or as direct as you were expecting, but it has been answered, and it's answered on the basis that access was denied some months earlier and one house was temporarily occupied by Serbian police which kept these people from it. From that circumstance and the destruction of the village, the witness inferred that the village was occupied entirely or substantially by Albanian households. Now, he can't take that any further. That's his evidence; it may be right, it may be wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'll move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Abrahams, do you know when the fighting started in Lodja?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not precisely, but I believe roughly in July 1998 was the first major fighting. Certainly there were incidents in and around Pec prior to that, violent incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You are right in saying that the operations commenced in July. My apologies. Did any of the individuals you interviewed tell you that the KLA had attacked the house belonging to the family of the Ujosevics on the 6th of July, 1998, in the village of Lodja?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that particular allegation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know that several Serb policemen were injured and that two were abducted by the KLA in July of 1998?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that there were hostilities at that time, but I was not aware -- or I would have to check my records to answer your question whether I was aware of the details about those hostilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Abrahams. But it is not a detail to learn that Lodja was taken by the KLA in early 1998.

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's correct. Lodja was taken by the KLA, and there was an action to re-take Lodja. Lodja is quite close to Pec. It could be considered a suburb of Pec, even, and no doubt the authorities were deeply concerned about the KLA's actions and took to re-take control of Lodja.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you hear at the time or at a later stage that Operation Lodja was considered to be one of the greatest successes of the Kosovo Liberation Army in the course of 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that claim.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Fine. As an individual who was knowledgeable and an expert about the area in the last -- in the recent periods, did you in the last seven or eight years read any of the publications describing this particular period, that's to say the month of July of 1998, in Lodja?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically with regards to Lodja, I'm not aware of any material, but of course I did follow and I continue to follow the various research and publications about the Kosovo conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you familiar with the name of Tahir Zemaj?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps read the book "Thus Spake Tahir Zemaj"?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that book.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know that Tahir Zemaj took part in Operation Lodja in July of 1998?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not heard that before.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you hear that Mr. Haradinaj had taken part in the operation?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have also not heard about Mr. Haradinaj's participation, but he was, of course, a commander in that region, so it would not surprise me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Abrahams.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up D002-6040. The next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Abrahams, when you were in Lodja in February of 1999 and you went through the place, did you come across such trenches, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, I may be mistaken here, but I believe this document was not on my learned colleague's list of exhibits to be used with this witness. I know different e-mails were sent quite late, but I did not see this specific document listed on their list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's certainly one that we have seen, Ms. Kravetz, in the course of earlier evidence. Carry on, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Madam Kravetz. We sent you a supplementary notification containing the two documents you were notified of earlier as well as of this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you recall my question, Mr. Abrahams?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall seeing trenches in Lodja, but it's certainly possible they were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we turn to the next page, please. Further on, please. It's not the one. Can we call up D002-6044, please. The next page, please. Further on, please. Still further on. The next photograph, can we see if that's the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Abrahams, when you were there, did you perchance see this house in the village of Lodja?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up Exhibit P754, page 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Abrahams, can you tell us when was it that these houses were damaged?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to check my notes to answer that question. The photo was taken in February 1999, so it's my belief it was in January or February of that year, but my memory fails me at this point. I would have to check my records.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What village is this? Can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is on the outskirts of Suva Reka town.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, and the name of the village is Restane; am I right?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that is correct. I'd have to check to be sure, but I believe that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you receive information from the individuals you interviewed that there was fighting around Restane in the course of the summer of 1998?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was fighting here and in Lodja. In no way am I denying that fighting took place. There was an armed conflict going on in many parts of Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you rule out the possibility that the damage was caused during the armed conflicts between the KLA and the Serbian forces?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the case of Lodja, we reached the conclusion that we could rule that out, that to me the destruction in Lodja appeared to have been systematic and not as a result of the fighting. To be more precise, many of the homes had one supportive column knocked out, which brought the second floor of the home down. This was seen repeatedly in many of the structures, and to us that appeared as if it had been deliberately knocked down by heavy machinery and not a result of combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were we able to see what you've just described for us in one of the photographs?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And I'm referring to Lodja, that the supporting column had been -- had been knocked down and that that was why the houses caved in. Was it something we were able to see on one of the photographs?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And you're an expert in statics to be able to draw such a conclusion?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I reached that conclusion based on my observations.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We were discussing Restane when you referred back to Lodja again. What are your conclusions with regard to Restane?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It was you who referred back to Lodja I think when we were dealing with Restane, but that is beside the point. You're now going to Restane. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were already discussing Restane when Mr. Abrahams -- when answering my question referred back to Lodja, but no matter. Let us go back to Restane now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I must refer to my notes and reports to answer your question in detail because I don't remember the specifics of Restane. However, I do recall reaching the conclusion that these homes had been purposely set on fire from within. I do not remember seeing any forensic evidence of combat, such as bullet marks on the external walls of these homes, trenches, or other signs of military activity. I recall seeing scar marks or burn marks from the interior of these homes, the destruction of the wooden roofs, but the walls and chimneys still standing, which to me indicated fire from within.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Abrahams, this picture was taken at least five months after the incident, and as far as I can see on this building that has no roof, you can see the laundry being hung out to dry. Somebody is obviously doing something in there, which means that at the time when this photograph was taken the scene of the crime had been changed, and I don't see why there should be any ammunition there. Somebody must have cleared it in the intervening six months.

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to check my records to accept your claim that this photograph was taken at least five months after the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at page 8 of the same exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Abrahams, what do we see on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a destroyed mosque in the Drenica region.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us more specifically what has been destroyed on this mosque?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this photograph, it is the top of the minaret and the roof of the structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us when this damage was inflicted on the mosque?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to check my records for that, but my recollection is during the offensive in September 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What is this place, please?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The precise location is -- I'm not sure of. It's in the Drenica area around the Obrinje village. It was Obrinje-Golubovac-Likovac - I believe Drenovac, but I don't recall the exact location. I can get that information for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Abrahams, as a serious researcher of the Human Rights Watch, I would like to ask you: How is it possible that you take a photograph without indicating the location, the time when the photograph was taken? Instead, now you have to go and try to jog your memory about all that.

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of that information on location and date is in my records.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us yesterday -- or, rather, let us go back to this image. Are any other buildings damaged on this photograph apart from the one that you've brought our attention to? Of course, I'm talking about visible damage.

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But can you rule out the possibility that at the time when this damage was -- when the mosque was damaged that there was a firing position located there in the mosque?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: A firing position in the mosque itself?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In or on the mosque.

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to check my records to answer precisely, but I am not aware of any testimony from individuals I interviewed about firing from within or near mosques.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Abrahams, you told us yesterday that you talked to a person who was a survivor of the incident in the Bela Crkva river-bed; am I right?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It's the incident that occurred in 1999 at the time when the air-strikes in Kosovo and Metohija or in Serbia already began; am I right?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And you told us that this person had an injury to the shoulder that was caused by a bullet or a round of some sort.

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right when I say that this interview was done either in Albania or in Macedonia? I don't know exactly where it was, but could you please tell me?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In northern Albania, in Kukes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your assistance. Am I right if I say that you took this person to see a doctor to have the bullet removed?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. We helped this person get to Tirana, where he received medical care.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And as a researcher, did you take a photograph of this person with the injury on the shoulder while you were interviewing him?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to check my records to answer precisely, but I do recall very well that this individual was extremely scared. He was concerned for his own safety, having been the surviving witness of a serious crime, and was therefore cautious about his identity being known at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, we'll get to that, but in 2002 in your interview with the OTP, you invoked Rule 70 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, but at that time it had nothing to do with that. You saw this injured person, you talked to him, and you took him to a doctor. Did you see any such photographs - you say that you did not remember - but anyway, did you see any photographs of this person with the injury yesterday or today in the course of the trial?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you tell me, did the doctor that treated that person, who operated on this person, did you take any medical records about the kind and severity of the injury, describing the injury?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us that after the hostilities ended in 1999 you went to Kosovo and Metohija. Can you tell us when you went there?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I first went to Kosovo after the hostilities in July 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you remember how long you stayed there in 1999?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that trip, approximately three weeks. I returned again I believe in November of that year.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember whether you were alone in July 1999 or were you accompanied by a colleague?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From approximately July 1999 throughout the rest of the year, we had a near-permanent presence in Kosovo, a small office staffed by my colleague Benjamin Ward. In addition, some other colleagues such as Martina Vandenberg who investigated the rape cases, came to Kosovo during that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I can conclude, then, that you went there on your own and that you encountered these other people in Kosovo, where they already were.

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And in November 1999, how long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly three weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me, how many people did you personally interview in July 1999 when you were there for three weeks?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The precise number is in my records and in a database of the interviews we created, but definitely at least 50.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You personally, I'm asking you about you yourself, not all of the officials who were in Kosovo. Did you personally conduct the 50 interviews that you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to check the database, which is readily available, to give you a precise number; but yes, I believe it was roughly 50, let's say, roughly 50.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how many interviews did you conduct in November 1999?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number; less than that, because in November 1999 I focused more on one incident, namely, killings in the Dubrava prison, and also during that time on abuses against Serbs by ethnic Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you please tell me, you were in Kosovo and Metohija in February 1999 when those photographs were taken. How long did you stay there at that time?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, the precise dates are available but my best recollection is approximately two weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how many people did you interview at that time?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to check my records to answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you recall how many people you spoke to from the 25th of March or, rather, the time when you arrived there in April, when you arrived to Albania, until the end of your stay in Macedonia and Albania? How many people did you yourself personally interview?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We created a database of every single interview, so I have to refer to that data to give you a precise answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I -- the reason why I'm asking you these questions is because you gave me the initial figure and bearing in mind the fact that in your statement I read that from the first time that you arrived there until the end of 1999 that you interviewed around 600 people all told and that many researchers worked on the project --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, I just wanted to ask my learned colleague for a reference where the witness says in his statement that he interviewed around 600 people in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't say in 1999 but from the moment he arrived in Kosovo for the first time, that was in May 1998, until the end of 1999, when he spoke to people in the field. To be quite honest, I don't have the exact reference. I will be able to look it up during the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But is it right that the Human Rights Watch interviewed this number of people and that this was a sample that you used for your subsequent analysis?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be accurate, the period March 24 through December 1999 when we researched specifically the violations during the NATO bombing period, March 24th to June 12th, that research by me and my colleagues involved approximately 600 interviews. Our conclusions are based primarily on those 600 interviews about the period of the NATO bombing, and all the interviews we cite are footnoted in "Under Orders" with the place and date, but we also created a database of all those interviews. So I could give you the total number, the number that was done by me as well as by all my colleagues, the date and place. All of that is available if it is helpful to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you are not saying that the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You are now saying that the 600 interviews that served as a basis for "Under Orders" were conducted from the beginning of the NATO air-strikes against Serbia until the end of 1999?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interviews that formed the basis for the sections in "Under Orders" that deal with the period of NATO bombing come to approximately 600.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now tell me how many people you yourself interview from May 1998 until March 1999, when the bombing started?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to go through my records to answer that question. I don't know. I can give you an estimate, but I don't know for sure. It's all in my notes. I can tell you I have five or six notebooks in total. The total must come in the hundreds.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us that in July you came in Kosovo and Metohija. Do you remember when was it that you left for Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the date. It's available in "Under Orders" when I conducted the interviews. That information is available but not -- I'm not recalling it at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But you recall quite well the dates that were mentioned by witnesses about the events in Meja; am I right?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Meja events were on April 27th. That's the date of the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And the photographs were taken in June, and you don't think that the crime scenes were not changed between the time when the crimes that the witnesses told you about were committed until the time when you took the photographs?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which photographs are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about the photograph that you took in Meja and you say that there were also some bodies that you saw lying by the road. Did you photograph those bodies?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those photographs were taken by my colleague Joanne Mariner.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So you didn't take photographs in Djakovica, Meja in July 1999?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to check my records to answer accurately.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, regardless of who took the photographs, what reliable way did you use to determine whether a body that was on the photograph actually was there since April or May 1999?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not prepared to make any comment on the length of time which that body was lying there, not having been there myself. I have to consult with "Under Orders" to give you a more precise answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But yesterday, Mr. Abrahams, you told us that there was a striking similarity between the statements you took in Albania from persons that you interviewed and your findings in the village of Meja where you actually found those bodies lying by the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would again ask my colleague for a reference where the witness yesterday said he found bodies lying by the road. That is not my recollection of his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my associate will find this part of the transcript from yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. While that's happening, Mr. Abrahams, perhaps you could remind the Chamber, is it your recollection that you did find bodies lying by the road in Meja?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, my colleague Joanne Mariner did when she entered a few days after the war stopped, June 14th approximately, but I myself did not. I entered Meja in July and did not witness any of those bodies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will be able to find that, but it's immaterial because we have the transcript for yesterday and the answer from today, and then it will be up to the Judges to give proper weight to both.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Abrahams, you say that while you were in the area around Djakovica that you spoke to the villagers about the NATO air-strikes. Did I hear you correctly? Did you say that yesterday?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We spoke to the residents of Djakovica and the surrounding villages about all events and incidents during the period of NATO bombing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you ask NATO to provide you reports as to what the targets were around Djakovica in this period, from the 24th of March until the 20th of June?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We produced a detailed report about NATO's conduct during the war, which resulted in civilian deaths, and my colleagues who conducted that research did communicate with NATO, to the best of my knowledge, about those matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ask the Yugoslav and Serbian authorities to provide you with the details about NATO air-strikes in that area where you were and where you were conducting your inquiries in and around Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And those reports of the Serbian authorities, are they contained in your report, "Under Orders"?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information is provided in most detail in the report about the NATO conduct. I forget the title of that report precisely, but it documents approximately 90 incidents in which roughly 500 civilians in Serbia died as a result of NATO bombing, and the main conclusions of that report are reproduced in "Under Orders."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think it is time for our technical break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will have the second break now and resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Abrahams, regarding the events in Djakovica and the area around it in 1999, in March and in subsequent months, did you talk to any ethnic Serbs?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: By that point, in Djakovica the Serbian community was small to not existent, having left or been kicked out of the area by the -- by ethnic Albanians, but we did speak with some Serbs and particularly in Prizren, which is -- had a larger population.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please correct me if I'm wrong, but in this publication of yours, "Under Orders," I can see that the date of publication is 2001.

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And by October 2001, you were unable to find any ethnic Serbs from Djakovica in the area around it to verify the information that you had.

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to check my records as to whether we interviewed any Serbs from the Djakovica area. I don't recall at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You gave a statement to the investigators of this Tribunal in March 1999; am I right?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like us to look at Exhibit P738, and I apologise in advance if I am wrong and if I fail to get the right page number because this is a 92 bis statement that contains three statements in itself. But I was really careful when preparing the references. Could we please have page 11 in the English version? I'm reading. These are references for the 92 bis package, or, rather, the page numbers go from 41 to 1, and they're handwritten, and this should be page 11 in the 1999 statement. That's 31, so I need 11. Well, my associate tells me that it's actually page 38. No, that's not the one. It says here 4. I need page 31.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Abrahams, yes, here in paragraph 2 of your statement, you say: "On the 23rd of June, 1998, I also interviewed a number of injured soldiers in Tirana ..." and you say that you provided the details of these witnesses to the International Criminal Tribunal. Do you see this at the end of paragraph 2? "On 23rd of June, 1998, I also ..."

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether you heard from those persons how they got injured?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to check my notes to answer your question, but assumedly that would have been a question of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you don't even know the place where they were injured?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that information is available, but in my notes and not in my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Very well. And you go on to say that you provided the details to the International Tribunal about those witnesses. Could you please tell us, when did you provide those details? I assume that this was handed over to the Office of the Prosecutor of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall when. I believe these would have been -- this information would have been provided to one of the investigators and probably one of the investigators that took my statement, but I'm not sure about that fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So the investigator states in the statement itself that you gave him those details.

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't see that reference in here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 2: "I have provided the details of these witnesses to the ICTY."

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then I certainly did. I just don't recall to whom exactly I provided the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what I'm asking you. Did you before making this statement provide those details to the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you please tell me, did you notify the public that the injured KLA members were being treated in the Republic of Albania?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that information is in our reports, but certainly I spoke publicly about it on numerous occasions. The KLA's presence in northern Albania was no secret and certainly something that we spoke about openly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you speak openly about the training centres that the KLA ran in Albania?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and have continued to speak openly about some of those centres including detention facilities that they maintained in parts of Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you speak about the arms smuggling from Albania into Kosovo and Metohija in 1998?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, repeatedly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And did the Human Rights Watch make a valued judgement of the conduct of the Republic of Albania vis-a-vis the situation in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean by a valued judgement?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, did they take a position in accordance with the international law -- whether it is in accordance with the international law to smuggle arms, treat members of one warring side, and have training centres in its territory while at the same time there was a conflict going on in the neighbouring state? You are an expert in international politics.

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, northern Albania at that time was a largely lawless region where a lot of uncontrolled activity went on. So the training centres, detention facilities, and arms smuggling that took place and existed and took place during that time, which definitely did take place during that time, were to a large extent out of control of the Albanian government. That being said, I am convinced -- it is my opinion that the Albanian government knew about the existence of the KLA and its activities and did not take efforts to stop it. That is my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please scroll up a little bit. I want to see the page of this statement to be able to orient myself. Is it uploaded into the system as page 11 or page 4 because that will enable me to give you a proper reference because obviously my records are not in line with the way that it is recorded in the system.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That, Your Honours, in e-court is page 31.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now my reference is supposed to be page 9 in the English version of this statement made in 1999, so that would be page 37 now, then. I'm sorry. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Abrahams, paragraph 5 from the top, the last sentence: "... I observed a similar pattern: The army shelled from a distance to force the villagers to flee, and then the police moved in on foot." Can you tell us, were you an eye-witness of the pattern you refer to here at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The case that I witnessed to shelling would be Gornje Obrinje in September 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You were in the village as the shelling was going on?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thankfully, no. I was in Plocica and Mlecan on that day observing -- or hearing -- hearing the sounds of artillery fire and observing Gornje Obrinje in the distance on fire, at least the -- I could see the smoke coming out from the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you also able to see the police entering the village of Obrinje?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If the interpretation I got was right, the portion of the text I read out to you was that you said: "In a number of villages that I visited where I conducted research, I observed a similar pattern ..." In other words, you observed a pattern which the police forces consistently adopted; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Abrahams, did it seem to you that this same story was told over and over again by all the witnesses who were interviewed by Human Rights Watch?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The witnesses whose statements you took, did they state the same thing in their statements, that the police would first encircle a place, shell it, and then proceed to enter it?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every witness statement is unique and reflects the observations of the individual being interviewed. In general, I detected a pattern of behaviour by the Serbian police and Yugoslav Army based on these interviews. And to us, this suggested a standard operating procedure because we saw it repeated in so many villages throughout Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Abrahams, did you perhaps read the indictment issued against Mr. Slobodan Milosevic or the indictment in the case of Milutinovic et al. or the indictment against the accused Djordjevic, in the present case?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have read the indictment against Slobodan Milosevic and Milan Milutinovic et al., but I have not read the indictment against the accused in court today.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will ask you about one part which talks about the underlying crimes or where it is also stated that the Serbian forces encircle villages, shell them, and then proceed to enter them. Is this something that you noticed or found in the two indictments that you read?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure how to answer that question. I read those indictments, and if this citation is indeed taken from them, then I would have read that line as well. But I'm not sure what you're asking me. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm simply asking you about the pattern of behaviour concerning the underlying crimes, where the Serbian forces would encircle a village, shell it, enter a village, and then proceed to do what the indictment alleges they did. Did you read something of the sort in these indictments?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall every detail of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on. Mr. Abrahams, you told us yesterday that you heard from an Albanian journalist who worked for "Koha Ditore" that something had been going on in Gornje Obrinje and that therefore you went there on the 29th of September, 1998; is my understanding correct?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Looking at your March 1999 statement, which should be the portion at page 38 -- I hope I'm right -- no. I will find the precise reference for you, and we'll read out what it is. That's page 34. That should be the second paragraph from the bottom, Mr. Abrahams. "On the evening of the 28th of September, I heard reports of incidents at Obrinje ..." Have you found the paragraph? That's the second paragraph from the bottom [In English] -- 28th.

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does this part of your statement say that you had heard of the incidents at Gornje Obrinje on the 28th of September at the American embassy at KDOM and that you had heard there that something had been going on at Obrinje?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can clarify. I first heard about the alleged incident on September 28th in the evening, and the next morning my colleague and I went to the office of the KDOM. It's the Kosovo Diplomatic Observer Missions. It had three components: EU, Russian, and American, and we went to the American component. We went there to see whether they had any information about this incident, and indeed, they told us that they did. They did not provide any details, but they said, Yes, we are aware that something took place in that area. So that was a further reason for us to pursue the topic and visit the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you cooperate with the US KDOM office?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not. But maybe you should clarify what you mean by "cooperate" so I can be precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, for instance, by exchanging information, you giving them information, they giving you information.

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had no cooperation on a formal level, but in an informal way, as this exchange on September 29th indicates, they were at times willing to provide us with very basic and rudimentary information, such as, Yes, we are aware that something took place in that village. But they never provided anything in any way of a more substantive nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you provide them with information that you had in order to ensure that they are kept abreast as an observer mission?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We undertook no specific efforts to inform or update the KDOM of US, EU, or Russia, but all of our reports and statements were made available to them, as they were to all diplomatic and international representatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In view of the standing of the Human Rights Watch, did you have knowledge about the nature and the extent of relations of the higher levels of Human Rights Watch with the US KDOM or the other office or other international organisations that were involved in this process in that period of time?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the responsible Balkans researcher at that time, I would have been aware of any communication between my organisation and international organisations or governments.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's turn to the following page of the English version. Paragraph 3, Mr. Abrahams, do you see the sentence which says: "Some people who told us what they believed had happened ..." That's right?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: There you say, Mr. Abrahams: "Some people who told us what they believed had happened had run away when police came. They had not seen the incidents themselves." Is that right? Is that indeed what you said in your statement, Mr. Abrahams?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right if I say that you yourself did not testify to the incidents at Gornje Obrinje either?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the actual killings, no, I was not a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right if I say that fighting was going on at Gornje Obrinje between the KLA and the Serbian forces?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was fighting going on on the -- at least the 25th and 26th, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right if I say that the KLA forces withdrew from Gornje Obrinje into the woods?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of the precise movements of the KLA, but generally speaking, when faced with greater fire-power they did retreat into -- away from the combat areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Again, we're coming to an area of a pattern, Mr. Abrahams. In the course of your research, did you observe the fact that the pattern of able-bodied men fleeing villages upon the sight of Serbian forces arriving and taking to the woods?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was common for ethnic Albanian men to flee their villages when they saw security forces advancing, usually, they said, out of fear of what would happen to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let's talk specifically about 1998. Did the state of Serbia -- or was the state of Serbia or the state of Yugoslavia as affluent as that it would shell villages without there being any fighting and that this should happen over and over again?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot comment as to the affluence of the Serbian or Yugoslav state, but I did document a pattern of indiscriminate fire into villages as well as serious crimes including executions after forces entered those villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this: Why would something be shelled or fired upon in the situation where a village can be entered without any shelling? If no resistance is put up, then other means can be used to enter a village. Will you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why shelling was used, but I'm also not denying that the KLA was present in some villages in question. I'm not denying that the KLA engaged in hostilities against Serbian and Yugoslav forces. I'm also not denying that the KLA repeatedly violated international humanitarian law in its own actions, but none of that justifies the unlawful behaviour of the Serbian and Yugoslav forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Once again, we've come into the realm of opinions, but it will be up to the Trial Chamber to assess that. Am I right if I say, Mr. Abrahams, that you were communicating with some individuals from the Finnish forensic team which was supposed to carry out an exhumation at Gornje Obrinje?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you pin-point when exactly it was that you were in contact with members of the Finnish forensic team?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to check my records to be sure, but I believe I spoke with members of that team in November and maybe December 1999 when they were attempting to enter Gornje Obrinje to conduct an exhumation, but they were blocked by the Serbian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. According to my information, it was on the 10th of December that the Finnish forensic team together with an investigating judge of the Pristina district court and a deputy of the public prosecutor, together with the police, set out for Obrinje to carry out an exhumation of the bodies at Gornje Obrinje. Did you have that sort of information too?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have information to the effect that next to the village of Trstenik close to Gornje Obrinje, the convoy which was supposed to carry out the exhumation was pulled over or stopped because a KLA check-point was present nearby?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of the details of the incident you are suggesting, but I do recall speaking with a member of the forensic team who said that the Serbian police had restricted the movement of the forensic team.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know which member of the forensic team that was? Can you name him?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to check my notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you aware that in relation to this failed attempt at exhumation, both the KDOM and the OSCE were informed?

utterances.speaker: FREDERICK CRONIG ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of what information came to KDOM or the OSCE.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think our time for this session is up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djurdjic. We must now adjourn for the day, to continue tomorrow at 2.15 in the day. Again, an officer of the court will give you more detailed instructions. There is no particular matter that requires attention at the moment, so we will simply adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 7th day of May, 2009, at 2.15 p.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
